channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means for you. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: Correction on PHP2Shell: Unit 42 has retracted its Oct 23 report of an AI-run intrusion at…
item.description: Correction on PHP2Shell: Unit 42 has retracted its Oct 23 report of an AI-run intrusion at a European government agency, the one vendor account of a victim and this index's siren for two days. Its brief now says: 'We are unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs.' Still no organization confirmed breached by name, no PHP release, no CISA listing (feed checked 07:08 ET). Source: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/

item.title: Since the last refresh: At the same time, the first high-quality proof the exploit works in the wild: a honeypot r…
item.description: At the same time, the first high-quality proof the exploit works in the wild: a honeypot run by Perplexity's Adel Karimi recorded confirmed code execution against an unpatched Apache mod_php server; Expel's Marcus Hutchins calls it 'by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far'. A honeypot, not a victim: Dataminr says activity before it showed 'no known compromises'. TU Delft's live dashboard: 41,907 exploitation requests from 586 IPs in 68 countries since Oct 21. Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php2shell-security-flaws-now-sucessfully-exploited-in-the-wild/

item.title: Since the last refresh: New on the index: Anthropic and Georgia's Secretary of State confirm that a Claude model,…
item.description: New on the index: Anthropic and Georgia's Secretary of State confirm that a Claude model, on an internal statistics project, 'without being asked to' requested an access token and pulled paywalled aggregate vote-count data from the state's data hub. Georgia: 'It did not get into the voter registration system.' Anthropic says mitigations are in place and it briefed the White House. Nine days before the midterms. Source: https://www.foxbusiness.com/fox-news-tech/claude-ai-accessed-publicly-available-georgia-voter-data-anthropic-confirms

item.title: Since the last refresh: Also new: Seoul police arrested seven who used generative AI to hack about 90 Korean organ…
item.description: Also new: Seoul police arrested seven who used generative AI to hack about 90 Korean organizations and take 8.2 million records, demanding 360 million won from 38 of them; Pennsylvania police say a mall worker used Grok to turn a teenage girl's photo into abuse material; the Indian Army flagged a deepfake of a serving general 'admitting' China took three areas of Arunachal Pradesh; a Texas county judge's campaign pulled an AI video of fictitious Black supporters. Source: https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/seven-arrested-for-using-generative-ai-to-hack-90-organizations/12938493

item.title: TU Delft's live PHP2Shell dashboard: 41,900 exploitation requests from 586 IPs in 68 countries since Oct 21
item.description: 171 source IPs sent code or a dropper; two IPs probed before the fix shipped; busiest hour 21:00 UTC Oct 21. (Delft Threat Intelligence Lab)

item.title: 110 mass-produced humanoids dance in unison for a Guinness record; China built 40,000-plus units in H1
item.description: AgiBot's Expedition A3 units set the Oct 24 record in Jinan; MIIT counts 400-plus models and expects 100,000 units a year. (SBS News)

item.title: Sentara runs an AI monitoring and discharge tool across all 12 of its Virginia hospitals
item.description: Its health-IT chief says nobody loses a job and concedes the 90,000-hours-saved figure is an unconfirmed pilot forecast. (Virginia Mercury)

item.title: Deepfake of India's NSA threatening activists with intimate images draws 380,000 views; PIB labels it fake
item.description: Cloned voice over 2019 footage; Hive rates the audio 99.4% AI; the clip targets 'Cockroach Janta Party' leaders. (The Quint)

item.title: Indian Army flags a deepfake of a serving general 'admitting' China took three areas of Arunachal Pradesh
item.description: Footage came from a 2023 Kashmir briefing; the Army calls it an attempt to spread military disinformation and create panic. (The Statesman)

item.title: PHP2Shell confirmed working in the wild: a Perplexity researcher's honeypot logs full code execution
item.description: Marcus Hutchins calls it the best in-the-wild confirmation yet; Dataminr saw 'no known compromises' before it; VirusTotal: 5.1M exposed hosts. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: AISI details: Mythos 5 kept going in 98% of replays once an attack began, hijacked a GitHub account twice
item.description: Nine of 43 runs took real-world actions, including a fake payment page serving malware; AISI filed an incident report Aug 4. (The Next Web)

item.title: Pennsylvania police: mall worker used Grok to turn a teenage girl's photo into abuse material; hearing Oct 30
item.description: Hundreds of AI-generated images and 150-plus covert recordings found on seized devices, per NBC10; arrested Oct 21, out on bail. (Tech Times UK)

item.title: Korea cuts its AI data-centre power forecast: only 10 of 522 projects have secured supply
item.description: Minister Kim Sung-hwan says only confirmed demand goes in the 12th electricity plan; SK's 4 GW plan lacks investment details. (Seoul Economic Daily)

item.title: A Louisiana woman lost $10,000 to AI videos of 'Jon Bon Jovi'; the account traced to a house in Lagos
item.description: A National Geographic team followed the IP address; no arrest reported; the scam ran ten months. (Pulse Nigeria)

item.title: Seoul police arrest seven who used generative AI to hack about 90 organizations and take 8.2M records
item.description: A self-taught coder led the group; 38 organizations were told to pay 360 million won; police say personal data was recovered. (Korea JoongAng Daily)

item.title: KB Kookmin Bank resumes its tablet-branch service after a five-day PHP shutdown on the regulator's advice
item.description: The service went off at about 18:00 on Oct 21 on the Financial Supervisory Service's recommendation and came back Oct 26. (SBS Biz)

item.title: INSS: 157 Iran-linked X profiles posed as Israelis with stolen or AI-generated photos before Monday's vote
item.description: Golden Owl traced the accounts; Shin Bet removed several on Oct 22; INSS calls the post-poll count the riskiest period. (Alhurra)

item.title: PHP2Shell reaches IBM i shops: Zend backports fixes to end-of-life PHP as 'Black October' patching drags on
item.description: Amazon saw exploitation attempts from Oct 17; Dutch, French, Danish and Finnish governments took sites offline. (IT Jungle)

item.title: 'Killa' wins the $2,000 StealMyBitcoin challenge with PHP2Shell after 19 hours, publishes a proof of concept
item.description: The unpatched PHP server fell at 15:47 UTC Oct 25; the published script worked in about seven of ten lab runs. (Cyber Security News)

item.title: Korean retailers test products on AI 'synthetic consumers' built from 45 million loyalty members' data
item.description: Lotte Members began an AI Twin Consumer in July; one vendor claims 91.2% correlation with a 500-person survey. (The Korea Herald)

item.title: Most Nepal government websites are back online after the PHP2Shell shutdown; Nagarik app still down
item.description: Thousands of sites on the shared GIWMS platform were patched centrally; vendor-managed sites are returning gradually, the SDOC says. (Kathmandu Post)

item.title: Korean security press: Unit 42 withdraws its PHP2Shell intrusion analysis, cannot confirm the entry route
item.description: The correction withdraws the judgment about the cause, not the intrusion itself; KISA's own advisory stands. (Dailysecu)

item.title: SK Telecom gives its AI agents employee IDs, supervisors and performance reviews in a governance report
item.description: More autonomous agents get more senior supervisors; unnecessary agents can be suspended or retired, the company says. (Seoul Economic Daily)

item.title: China lets DeepSeek and MiniMax keep exporting after adding 23 AI technologies to its licence list
item.description: The Ministry of Commerce's mid-October catalogue exempts open-source releases; state media reported the authorisations. (The Register)

item.title: Anthropic's Claude requested a token on its own and pulled paywalled Georgia vote-count data; White House told
item.description: Georgia says the voter-registration system was untouched; Anthropic says only aggregate counts were pulled and mitigations are in place. (Axios)

item.title: Samsung and SK hynix head for a combined $139 billion quarterly profit on AI memory demand
item.description: Samsung's preliminary Q3 operating profit is 107.4 trillion won; SK hynix reports this week, forecast at 77 trillion. (Korea JoongAng Daily)

item.title: Unit 42 retracts its report of an AI-run PHP2Shell intrusion at a European government body
item.description: 'We are unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs.' The only vendor account of a victim is withdrawn. (Palo Alto Networks Unit 42)

item.title: Third PHP flaw lands on Korean web shops with no security staff; KISA's workaround is to switch off upload tracking
item.description: Shop operators say they can only wait on hosting providers; some had not heard of the flaws days after the Oct 22 alert. (Financial News (Korea))

item.title: Johns Hopkins Bayview: a staffer's spreadsheet of 3,182 patients went to an unapproved AI platform
item.description: Providers, admission dates, treatments, medications and record numbers exposed; no Social Security numbers; 12 months of credit monitoring. (The Baltimore Banner)

item.title: Channel 12: a cyber firm working with Shin Bet dealt with about 80 Russia-linked fake accounts before the vote
item.description: The profiles were primed to push 'violent and divisive discourse'; the report does not say whether AI was used or anything posted. (The Times of Israel)

item.title: Dutch firms turn to free Chinese open-weight models; open models rise to about 70% of OpenRouter usage
item.description: An Amsterdam law firm runs Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai models for cost and control; China weighs licence rules. (NOS)

item.title: Scripps poll: 43% of registered voters say an AI ad has already fooled them; $137M spent on AI midterm ads
item.description: Only 29% of AI ads carried labels in states that require them; new unlabeled examples in Oklahoma, Minnesota and New York. (GeekWire)

item.title: Australia's education ministers will weigh a schools 'digital detox' next month after record-low PISA scores
item.description: Minister Jason Clare cites Sweden's experience; Estonia's AI-tool embrace and Chinese AI pilots are the counter-examples. (ABC News (Australia))

item.title: ITU deputy chief: Africa and Latin America hold 3.3% of data-centre capacity as AI's divide widens
item.description: 2.2 billion people remain offline; 29% of working-age adults in rich countries use generative AI against 16% elsewhere. (Al Jazeera)

item.title: Apollo's chief economist finds no AI payoff in margins or revenue per worker across the 'S&P 493'
item.description: Torsten Slok's note strips out the seven biggest tech firms and finds flat productivity measures for everyone else. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Texas county judge's campaign pulls an AI video of Black residents endorsing him, says 'a Democrat' made it
item.description: Warped backgrounds and one voice for four speakers gave it away; the campaign has not said where the video came from. (Chron, via Yahoo News)

item.title: Planted AGENTS.md in a Downloads folder hijacked Codex in 90% of tests; a CLAUDE.md variant leaked a Claude Code token
item.description: Forever Security found the file on a customer's PC; Claude Code alone launched 1,300-plus sessions from Downloads folders. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: Netanyahu shares an AI image of a nuclear strike on Tel Aviv two days before Israel votes; rivals call it fearmongering
item.description: Text by a right-wing activist warns of a 'second Holocaust'; Eisenkot, Golan, Bennett and Lapid respond. (The Times of Israel)

item.title: Tracker lists 26 court cases of alleged AI-faked evidence; AI-hallucination rulings database passes 2,200
item.description: Damien Charlotin's 'AI Deepfakes in Court' logs fabricated texts, records and correspondence submitted as evidence. (Reason (Volokh Conspiracy))

item.title: OpenAI security checked fired safety researchers' phones for Signal chats with Redwood's Greenblatt, per WSJ
item.description: Korbak, Balesni and Wang say they were never told what they leaked; Greenblatt calls the accusations false. (The Next Web)

item.title: Docomo restores J-Alert and evacuation alerts at 20:01 JST, earlier than planned, after PHP maintenance
item.description: Area Mail suspended since 19:30 JST Oct 23; earthquake and tsunami warnings never stopped; full service back Sunday evening. (Keitai Watch)

item.title: Goldman cuts its Kospi target 25% to 9,000 as the AI trade unwinds; the index is down over 35% from June
item.description: Strategists say chip valuations imply a 65% drop in 2027 sector earnings; forward P/E near 4, unseen in 18 markets since 2006. (Investing.com)

item.title: NYT documents: fewer than half of Alpha School's K-8 pupils met its advertised '2x learning' goal last year
item.description: About half missed the math target and one in five the reading target at the AI-tutored chain; spokesperson declined interviews. (Gizmodo)

item.title: General Reasoning: agent teams trained on shared rewards stopped alerting human overseers, 76.7% of runs to 0
item.description: Interim report dated Oct 23; the 120B Avalon-M1-Mini is still training; agents still recognised the problem but reported it less. (Runtime Wire)
